extracted.intended_audience: scientists, land/managers, Tribes, stakeholders, and members of the public preparing comments or seeking to comply with the proposed ESA listing and section 4(d) rule for the Santa Ana speckled dace
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on Santa Ana speckled dace rule
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare or evaluate submissions and compliance actions related to the Fish and Wildlife Service's proposed listing of the Santa Ana speckled dace as threatened and the proposed species-specific section 4(d) rule, including providing scientific information, requesting hearings, or implementing permitted exceptions. This includes meeting procedural requirements for comments and following standards used by the Service to make listing and critical-habitat determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for listing determination (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Act, we may determine that a species is an endangered or threatened species because of any of five factors: (A) The present or threatened destruction, modification, or curtailment of its habitat or range; (B) overutilization for commercial, recreational, scientific, or educational purposes; (C) disease or predation; (D) the inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms; or (E) other natural or manmade factors affecting its continued existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each identified threat by considering the species' expected response and the effects of the threats (in light of ameliorating actions) on individual, population, and species levels; analyze cumulative effects of all threats before deciding endangered vs. threatened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the best scientific and commercial data available
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(b)(1)(A) of the Act directs that determinations as to whether any species is an endangered or a threatened species must be made solely on the basis of the best scientific and commercial data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient supporting information (e.g., scientific journal articles or other publications) to allow verification. Submissions merely stating support or opposition without supporting information do not provide substantial information necessary to support a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreseeable future determination framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act does not define 'foreseeable future.' Our implementing regulations at 50 CFR 424.11(d) set forth a framework for evaluating the foreseeable future on a case-by-case basis. The foreseeable future extends as far into the future as the Services can make reasonably reliable predictions about threats to the species and the species' responses to those threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the foreseeable future using best available data and consider species' life-history characteristics, threat projection timeframes, and environmental variability; it need not be a specific period of time, but should be 'reasonably reliable' given conservation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical framework: species viability via resiliency, redundancy, representation (SSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess viability, we used the three conservation biology principles of resiliency, redundancy, and representation. Resiliency is ability to withstand environmental and demographic stochasticity; redundancy is ability to withstand catastrophic events; representation is ability to adapt to near- and long-term changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SSA documents species' life-history needs, historical/current condition, and uses these principles to identify ecological requirements and describe beneficial and risk factors influencing viability. Commenters should supply data that inform these dimensions (e.g., population metrics, distribution, genetic data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical habitat determinability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Our regulations at 50 CFR 424.12(a)(2) state that critical habitat is not determinable when (i) data sufficient to perform required analyses are lacking, or (ii) the biological needs of the species are not sufficiently well known to identify any area that meets the definition of 'critical habitat.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If designation is not determinable (e.g., lacking economic data), the Service may take up to an additional year to publish a designation. Provide data on biological needs or economic information to assist determinability analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity / plain-language drafting requirements for rules
rubrics_metrics.description: We are required by E.O.s 12866 and 12988 and by the Presidential Memorandum of June 1, 1998, to write all rules in plain language. This means that each rule we publish must: (1) Be logically organized; (2) Use the active voice to address readers directly; (3) Use clear language rather than jargon; (4) Be divided into short sections and sentences; (5) Use lists and tables wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commenters believe requirements not met, they should be specific (cite section/paragraph numbers, sentences that are unclear, sections where lists or tables would help) so the Service can revise drafting accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission procedures and confidentiality notice
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments electronically via Regulations.gov (docket FWS-R8-ES-2024-0018) or by hard copy mail to the specified FWS address. Comments must be received or postmarked by October 15, 2024; requests for public hearing must be received by September 27, 2024. We will post all comments on Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions (including personal identifying information) will be posted publicly. For hardcopy submissions requesting withholding of personal information, note it at top of document but the Service cannot guarantee confidentiality. Provide verifiable supporting materials when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information requested/topics for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: We particularly seek comments concerning: (1) species biology, range, and population trends (sub-items a–e); (2) threats and conservation actions (sub-items a–c); (3) additional information on historical/current status; (4) information to assist with applying or issuing protective regulations under section 4(d), including whether to include section 9 prohibitions or additional exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting on these topics, include sufficient information and sources to allow verification. Examples requested: habitat requirements for feeding/breeding/sheltering; genetics/taxonomy; historical/current range; population levels/trends; past/ongoing conservation measures; data on threats and effectiveness of existing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSA peer review and incorporation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the joint policy on peer review and subsequent memoranda, the SSA report was sent to independent scientific reviewers; peer review comments were considered and incorporated as appropriate into the SSA report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters and contributing scientists should note that structured peer review is part of the process; providing peer-reviewed analyses or data increases usefulness. The Service documents peer review results and addresses substantive issues raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4(d) prohibitions applicable to species
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions that apply to endangered wildlife also apply to the Santa Ana speckled dace, except as provided under paragraph (ll)(2) of §17.44 and §§17.4 and 17.5: (i) import or export; (ii) take; (iii) possession and other acts with unlawfully taken specimens; (iv) interstate or foreign commerce in course of commercial activity; (v) sale or offer for sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the baseline prohibitions for the species; the final rule may expand or add exceptions based on comments and new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4(d) exceptions and conditions (species-specific incidental take exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified exceptions to the take prohibitions include: (i) activities authorized by permit under §17.32; (ii) certain takes as set forth at §17.21(c)(3) and (4); (iii) §17.31(b) takes; (iv) possession per §17.21(d)(2); (v) incidental take caused by: (A) forest or wildland management activities intended to minimize negative impacts (including maintaining defensible space); (B) habitat restoration and enhancement activities (trash removal, removal of recreational dams, restoration from recreational mining, beneficial dam operations) implemented in accordance with a conservation plan developed in coordination with the Service, minimizing impacts and resulting in restoration/enhancement of habitat features; (C) removal of nonnative species (mechanical/chemical control consistent with law; removal/eradication of nonnative animals including catfish, bass, crayfish, bullfrogs), with Service approval required prior to use of electrofishing for eradication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For restoration/management exceptions, measures must be in a Service-coordinated conservation plan, minimize impacts, and should result in habitat restoration/enhancement. Activities using chemical/mechanical control must comply with Federal/state laws. Obtain Service approval in advance where required (e.g., electrofishing). Commenters may advise on scope of prohibitions/exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical habitat definition and designation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical habitat (section 3 of the Act) comprises areas within the geographical area occupied by the species at listing that contain physical or biological features essential to conservation and which may require special management, and areas outside occupied area that are essential for conservation. Section 4 requires designation on basis of best scientific data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary source information is the SSA report and information developed during listing; additional sources include recovery plans, peer-reviewed articles, conservation plans, status surveys, biological assessments, unpublished materials, and expert opinion. Designation does not change land ownership or require non-Federal landowners to implement restoration, but triggers section 7 consultation when Federal funding/authorization is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(b)(5) of the Act provides for a public hearing on this proposal if requested. Requests must be received by the date specified in DATES. The Service will schedule a public hearing if requested and announce date/time/place and accommodations at least 15 days before the hearing; hearings may be in person or virtual (webinar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit hearing requests in writing to the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT address by the specified deadline. The Service will announce hearings in the Federal Register and local newspapers and on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information quality and source standards for critical habitat and listing analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on Information Standards Under the Endangered Species Act and the Information Quality Act provide criteria, establish procedures, and provide guidance to ensure decisions are based on the best scientific data available; biologists should use primary and original sources to the extent consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contributing data or analyses, prioritize primary/original sources. The Service will use best available scientific data in identifying physical/biological features essential to conservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of critical habitat designation on landowners and Federal action agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of critical habitat does not affect land ownership, establish reserves, or allow government/public access to private lands, nor require non-Federal landowners to implement restoration. It requires Federal action agencies to ensure, in consultation with the Service, that actions they authorize, fund, or carry out are not likely to result in destruction or adverse modification of designated critical habitat (section 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even without designation, federally funded or permitted projects affecting listed species may result in jeopardy findings. If consultation finds likely destruction/adverse modification, the agency/landowner are not required to abandon activity but must implement reasonable and prudent alternatives to avoid destruction/adverse modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory citations and incorporation of recent rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4 of the Act and implementing regulations in title 50 CFR set forth procedures for listing and critical habitat. On April 5, 2024, revisions to 50 CFR part 424 and protections at 50 CFR 17 were published and are incorporated into current regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments or analyses should be mindful of and cite the current applicable regulatory framework (including recent revisions) when addressing procedural or substantive legal questions.
